entities.summary:
Michele Morosini was the 61st Doge of Venice, serving just 4 months from 10 June 1382 until his death on 16 October the same year.

As a member of the powerful Morosini family, Michele Morosini was born into a life of politics and power, with his ancestors having held significant influence in the Venetian Republic. His rise to doge was swift, but his tenure was marked by controversy and power struggles.

Morosini's legacy is complex, reflecting the tumultuous nature of his time. His short reign was marked by a series of struggles with the nobility and the rising power of the Great Council. Despite his efforts, Morosini was unable to quell the unrest, and his dogate came to an abrupt end. His death was a catalyst for further instability in Venice, paving the way for the Black Death's devastating impact on the city.

Morosini's story is a testament to the enduring power of family and politics in shaping the course of history.
